title: C-O7a: count the Planner's own usage from its transcripts into the pool, and `orchestrator pick planner` for the launcher
spec:
Why: the pool only counts tokens from worker JSON output (spawn.py run_claude usage), so the interactive Planner session, the largest consumer, is invisible; measured 2026-09-18: pool credited account A with 613k tokens while the Planner transcript of one session summed to about 7.8M by the same metric (input + output + cache_read/10). The user then hit the subscription limit with no warning and no switch. (1) pool.py: Pool.tally_planner(now=None): for each account, find transcripts under <config_dir>/projects/<encoded ORCH_ROOT>/*.jsonl (the encoding replaces '/' with '-', e.g. -Users-k3ntaw-code-orchestrator; derive it from ROOT, do not hardcode); read only lines of type "assistant" whose timestamp falls in the current day and in the current 5-hour window (window_started in pool_state); sum message.usage.input_tokens + output_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens // 10 exactly as run_claude does; store per account planner_day_tokens and planner_window_tokens plus a per-file byte offset in pool_state so each tick reads only appended bytes (files are append-only JSONL; a shrunken file resets its offset). Account.utilization and the daily-budget check include the planner numbers. Malformed lines are skipped, never fatal. (2) daemon.tick(): call pool.tally_planner() at the start of each tick, wrapped like the stages (a failure prints one stderr line). (3) status(): each account shows planner_day_tokens and the window utilization including them; `orchestrator status --plain` prints them too. (4) cli.py: `pick <role>` (role in planner|scout|review|execute) prints the id and config_dir of the account pool.pick(role) returns, or exits 3 with "hold: no account with headroom", so the launcher outside this repo can start the Planner on the right account. README.md: one paragraph "Planner usage is counted from transcripts" and the `pick planner` line under Run it. Tests: tests/test_pool.py builds a fake config_dir with two JSONL files (assistant lines in and out of the window, a malformed line, a user line), asserts the sums, the offset resume on a second call, the utilization change and the pick result flipping to B when A's planner usage crosses the cap; tests/test_cli.py covers pick output and exit 3.
(Recreated from T-0107: re-pointed at the recreated C-O4)
acceptance: tests/test_pool.py: tally_sums_assistant_usage_in_window, tally_skips_malformed_and_user_lines, tally_resumes_from_offset, tally_raises_utilization_and_flips_pick; tests/test_cli.py: pick_prints_account_and_config_dir, pick_exits_3_when_none; all green
`orchestrator status --plain` shows planner_day_tokens per account after a tick in a test fixture
No transcript content other than usage numbers and timestamps is read into memory beyond the current line, and nothing from transcripts is written to the bus or logs
`uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests` green; no new dependency

result.summary: superseded by C-O7a v2 (next id after C-O5 v2): spec review T-0163 requested changes (transcript project-dir encoding also maps '.' to '-', planner counters never reset on window/day rollover, pick must tally first, prune offsets of deleted files). Specs are immutable, so recreated.

spec_review_risks.issue: Spec dictates deriving the transcript project-dir name from ROOT by only replacing '/' with '-'. Claude Code's actual convention also replaces '.' with '-' (visible in ~/.claude*/projects/ as e.g. '-Users-k3ntaw--claude-mem-observer-sessions' for path '/Users/k3ntaw/.claude-mem-observer-sessions'). Since this orchestrator is installed into arbitrary target repos via `orchestrator install /path/to/target`, any ROOT path containing a dot will hash to the wrong directory name and tally_planner will silently read zero lines from a directory that doesn't exist — exactly the 'no warning, no switch' failure the task exists to fix, just moved one layer down.

Account.utilization() already resets window_tokens/window_started (and day_tokens/day) when the window/day rolls over. The spec's tally design is explicitly incremental — read only newly-appended bytes via a per-file byte offset and add their usage to planner_window_tokens/planner_day_tokens — but never says these two new counters get zeroed on the same rollover. Since old in-window lines are never re-read once the offset has passed them, nothing will ever subtract their contribution back out. Once real, planner_window_tokens is monotonically non-decreasing across window resets, permanently pinning utilization at/above cap (double counting of a kind: previous window's usage bleeds into every future window). Same problem for planner_day_tokens across day rollover. This is the state-that-never-decreases failure mode called out in the review brief.

`pick <role>` is meant to let an external launcher choose an account before starting the interactive Planner — the exact gap this task exists to close. The spec only says daemon.tick() calls pool.tally_planner(); it never says the `pick` subcommand does. A standalone `orchestrator pick planner` run (the launcher's use case) will pick against whatever planner_* numbers happen to be sitting in pool_state.json from the last daemon tick — stale or, on a fresh install/daemon restart, absent — defeating the purpose for the one caller that matters most.

Per-file byte offsets in pool_state persist forever once a transcript file is seen, including sessions Claude Code itself later rotates/deletes; nothing in the spec prunes offsets for files that no longer exist, so pool_state.json grows unboundedly over the life of an installation.
